name: Arrays & Hashing
whenToUse: Need O(1) lookups, frequency counts, complement pairs, or deduplication on sequences.
whyGoogle: Dominates phone screens and warm-ups; tests clean API usage and trade-off reasoning under time pressure.

name: Two Pointers
whenToUse: Sorted arrays, palindromes, pair sums, or shrinking/expanding windows from both ends.
whyGoogle: Shows you can optimize brute force to linear time with invariant reasoning.

name: Sliding Window
whenToUse: Contiguous subarray/substring with a constraint (sum, distinct chars, at most K replacements).
whyGoogle: Very common on strings and arrays; mirrors real log/stream aggregation problems.

name: Prefix Sums
whenToUse: Range sum queries, subarray sum equals K, or equilibriums on static arrays.
whyGoogle: Foundation for scalable analytics-style questions and DP transitions.

name: Stack
whenToUse: Matching brackets, monotonic next-greater/smaller, parse/evaluate expressions.
whyGoogle: Tests structured thinking for parsers and undo/redo style systems.

name: Linked List
whenToUse: In-place reorder, cycle detection, merge lists, or pointer manipulation.
whyGoogle: Less frequent but classic for pointer discipline and edge-case hygiene.

name: Binary Search
whenToUse: Sorted data, first/last occurrence, rotated arrays, or monotonic predicate on index.
whyGoogle: Google loves log-time reasoning on large datasets and search infrastructure.

name: Binary Search on Answer
whenToUse: Minimize maximum, maximize minimum, capacity/time limits with feasible check function.
whyGoogle: Separates strong candidates on scheduling and resource allocation style problems.

name: Intervals
whenToUse: Merge/overlap, insert, meeting rooms, sweep-line on timelines.
whyGoogle: Calendar, capacity, and SLA problems map directly to interval logic.

name: Heap / Top-K
whenToUse: K largest/smallest, streaming median, merge K sorted lists, scheduling by priority.
whyGoogle: Core for ranking, autoscaling, and priority-queue system design tie-ins.

name: Trees (DFS)
whenToUse: Path sums, LCA prep, validate BST, serialize, diameter, recursion on subtrees.
whyGoogle: Tree DFS is a daily bread question type for recursive decomposition.

name: Trees (BFS)
whenToUse: Level order, zigzag, right-side view, min depth, connect nodes at level.
whyGoogle: BFS models shortest path on unweighted trees and fan-out traversal.

name: Trie
whenToUse: Prefix search, autocomplete, word dictionary, XOR maximum on bit trie.
whyGoogle: Directly related to search indexes and string-heavy services.

name: Backtracking
whenToUse: Combinations, permutations, subsets, sudoku, partition with constraints.
whyGoogle: Tests pruning, state management, and explaining exponential vs optimized search.

name: Graphs (BFS)
whenToUse: Shortest path unweighted, multi-source BFS, grid as graph, level expansion.
whyGoogle: Graph BFS appears constantly in onsite loops and system path-finding.

name: Graphs (DFS)
whenToUse: Connected components, cycle detection, flood fill, path existence.
whyGoogle: Foundation for dependency analysis and reachability in large graphs.

name: Topological Sort
whenToUse: DAG ordering, course schedule, build order, alien dictionary.
whyGoogle: Models task pipelines, build systems, and dependency resolution.

name: Union-Find (DSU)
whenToUse: Dynamic connectivity, counting components, Kruskal-style edge grouping.
whyGoogle: Efficient grouping problems mirror cluster and network union scenarios.

name: Dijkstra / Weighted Shortest Path
whenToUse: Non-negative edge weights, K stops, network delay, cheapest flight within hops.
whyGoogle: Weighted graphs connect coding to maps, routing, and latency optimization.

name: DP (1D)
whenToUse: Fibonacci-style, house robber, decode ways, climbing stairs with constraints.
whyGoogle: 1D DP checks recurrence design and space optimization habits.

name: DP (2D)
whenToUse: Grid paths, edit distance, interleaving strings, two-sequence matching.
whyGoogle: 2D DP is a onsite staple for string and matrix optimization.

name: DP (Knapsack)
whenToUse: 0/1 knapsack, subset sum, partition equal subset, coin combinations with limits.
whyGoogle: Resource allocation with constraints; common follow-up to greedy failures.

name: DP (LIS / Patience)
whenToUse: Longest increasing subsequence, Russian doll envelopes, patience sorting trick.
whyGoogle: Shows advanced DP reduction and binary search pairing.

name: Greedy
whenToUse: Local optimal choices with proof sketch: intervals, jumps, task scheduling.
whyGoogle: Google expects you to justify greedy vs DP and cite counterexamples.

name: Bit Manipulation
whenToUse: XOR tricks, single number, bitmask DP subsets, count set bits.
whyGoogle: Shows low-level reasoning useful in performance-critical code paths.

name: Intervals + Greedy
whenToUse: Minimum arrows, non-overlapping intervals, meeting rooms II, sweep greedy.
whyGoogle: Scheduling and capacity questions heavily weighted in Google loops.
